topic.name: The Average Rate of Change of a Function

question.text: The number of machines infected by a computer virus is represented by the function $f(t) = 4t^3-2t^2+5t+11,$ where $t$ is the time, in days, since the virus was first detected. What is the average rate of growth of $f(t)$ over the first week?
question.explanation:
Let $f(t)=4t^3-2t^2+5t+11$ be the number of machines infected by the computer virus after $t$ days. To find the average rate of growth of $f(t)$ over the first week, we use the average rate of change formula on the interval $[0,7]$:

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta t} & = \dfrac { f(b) - f(a)}{b-a} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {f(7) - f(0)} {7 - 0}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\left[4(7)^3-2(7)^2+5(7)+11\right] - \left[4(0)^3-2(0)^2+5(0)+11\right]} {7}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac {1309} 7\\[5pt] & = 187 \end{align*}

Therefore, the average rate of growth over the first week is $187$ machines per day.

example.title: Calculating the Average Rate of Change: Word Problem

question.text:
Find an interval where the average rate of change of $f(x)$ equals $0$ given the following table of values of $f(x)\mathbin{:}$

$ x $ $\,-3\,$ $\,-1\,$ $\,0\,$ $\,2\,$ $\,4\,$ $\,6\,$ $\,9\,$
$ f(x) $ $\,7\,$ $\,-4\,$ $\,3\,$ $\,-4\,$ $\,1\,$ $\,5\,$ $\,-4\,$
question.explanation:
We have $\dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta x}=0$ if and only if $\Delta f = 0.$ So \begin{align*} & \Delta f = 0 \\ & f(b)-f(a) = 0 \\ & f(b)=f(a). \end{align*}

This means we have to find an interval $[a,b]$ such that $f(a)=f(b).$

Since $f(-1)=f(9)=-4,$ we conclude that $\dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta x}= 0$ on the interval $[-1,9].$

example.title: Determining the Interval Over Which the Average Rate of Change is Zero

question.text:
The table below lists values of $f(x)$ at distinct $x$-values. Knowing that the average rate of change of the function $f(x)$ on the interval $[3p,5]$ is $-2,$ find the value of $p.$

$ x $ $\,-10\,$ $\,-7\,$ $\, 3p\,$ $\,-2\,$ $\,0\,$ $\,1\,$ $\,5\,$
$ f(x) $ $\,12\,$ $\,8\,$ $\,11\,$ $\,-2\,$ $\,3\,$ $\,-16\,$ $\,-8\,$
question.explanation:
Using the formula for the average rate of change, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta x} &= \dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {f(5)-f(3p)}{5- 3p} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-8-11}{5-3p} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-19}{5-3p}. \end{align*}

Now, we know that $\dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta x}=-2$ on the interval $[3p,5].$ Thus, \[ \dfrac{-19}{5-3p} = -2. \]

Solving for $p,$ we have

\begin{align} \dfrac{ -19}{5-3p} &= -2 \\[5pt] -19 &= -2\cdot(5-3p) \\[5pt] -19 & = -10 + 6p\\[5pt] -19 +10 &= 6p \\[5pt] -9 &= 6p\\[5pt] \dfrac{-9}{6} & = \dfrac{6p}{6}\\[5pt] -\dfrac{3}{2} & = p. \end{align}

Therefore, we conclude that $p=-\dfrac{3}{2}.$
